newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c. bank in no hurry to lift official rates.
newsitem.headline: Polish c. bank in no hurry to lift official rates.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland is not expected to raise official interest rates for now but instead try to cool the country's surging domestic demand by rapidly raising market rates, analysts said on Thursday.

They said the NBP, trapped between fast-growing currency reserves and huge monetary outflows created by additional flood relief funding, may boost market rates some 100 to 150 basis points from the previous 14-day drainage benchmark rate of 22.58 percent.

"The NBP is now trying to push up market rates by raising its reverse-repo and NBP-bill yields but an official interest-rate rise may not come so quickly," said Andrzej Ladko, chief dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
On Thursday the central bank increased its seven-day reverse repo rate to 22.90 percent, while lifting its 91-day NBP-bills to 22.99 percent, up from the last month's 22.50 percent.
Last week central banker Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said that market rates would rise and that there was a very real possibility of an official interest-rate increase.

"Market rates must rise to contain additional demand from flood-related government spending...but official rates are not likely to rise until one-day rates climb above lombard (emergency interbank) levels," said Krzysztof Rybinski, chief economist at ING Bank in Warsaw.
"The central bank will first evaluate consequences of its market rate rise before moving official rates," Rybinski added.
The NBP has kept its official rates unchanged at 22 percent for the discount and 25 percent for the lombard for more than a year despite a five-percentage-point fall in inflation during this time.
Poland's economy has been speeding up despite fast-rising real rates and GDP grew more than eight percent in the second quarter of 1997, according to independent estimates.
This growth follows impressive 7.1 percent GDP rise in the first quarter and a 6.1 percent rise in all of 1996.

"The NBP is bound to increase official rates in the longer term as this is the only way to curb domestic demand now that the fiscal side has been loosened by additional funding for the flood relief," said Marek Jezierski, senior dealer at PBI SA. @

The government, wary of criticism just two months before parliamentary polls, has pushed through a bill which increased its credit line with the NBP in order to raise funds neccessary for flood relief and other budgetary spending more easily.
The government also intends to borrow some $600 million from various international bodies including the World Bank and the European Investment Bank to aid the flood relief efforts.

On Wednesday the IMF said the zloty's recent decline created room for an official interest-rate rise and said a volatile exchange rate within the 14-percent band would limit the scope of unwanted hot foreign capital inflows.
